assessment: Endothelial cells lining the inner side of blood vessels constitute the blood-tissue barrier via regulation of cell-cell junctions. The cell nucleus regulates endothelial cell behaviors, but it is unclear how the nucleus contributes to endothelial cell activities at the cell membrane. This study for the first time demonstrates that nuclear membrane protein SUN1 stabilizes endothelial cell-cell junctions far from the nucleus via regulation of microtubule dynamics and Rho GEF-H1 signaling, revealing long-range cellular communication important for vascular development and endothelial barrier function.
